title: The kit in every request
scenario:
Your studio makes images and captions for Tidewell, a refillable-bottle brand. The brand kit is written. Now you decide how it goes into every request.

The exhibit is our own sketch, not a vendor format. The sizes and page numbers are made up for this case.
exhibit:
Request layout today (every request)
  1. Job brief (new every time)
  2. Today's date and job number
  3. Kit card, about 400 words: look, rules, voice
  4. Anchor image
  5. tidewell-guide.pdf, 40 pages, pasted in full

Two lines that clash
  Kit card:         "Never use stock photos."
  Guide, page 31:   "Stock photos from the approved library are fine."

questions.prompt: Which order is best for every request?

options.text: Date and job number, then the kit card, then the anchor, then the brief, so each request is easy to trace.
options.explanation: OpenAI says content such as timestamps goes at the end. A date at the top changes the beginning of every request, so nothing can be reused.

options.text: The job brief first, since it changes and needs the most care, then the kit card and the anchor image.
options.explanation: A part that changes sits first, so no two requests share a beginning. The vendors reuse a beginning only when it matches exactly.

options.text: Kit card, then anchor, then the brief, and the date and job number go at the end, with the brief.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI and Anthropic both say stable material goes first. OpenAI puts timestamps and other changing content at the end.

options.text: Change the order of the kit parts a little each time, so the model does not get used to one order.
options.explanation: OpenAI says reuse needs the entire rendered prefix to match. A new order each time means the beginning never matches.

questions.prompt: The 40-page guide is pasted into every request. What is the better design?

options.text: Keep the 400-word card in every request. Make the guide a file that opens only when a job needs it.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says that until a Skill is triggered only its name and description are in context. OpenAI says the model sees the name and description and decides from them.

options.text: Paste the guide into every request anyway. Extra detail never hurts, and the model will skip what it does not need.
options.explanation: The model still reads all 40 pages every time. The docs describe loading a long book on demand so it does not fill the request.

options.text: Cut the guide to three lines and delete the rest, so that every request stays as small as possible.
options.explanation: That loses details people need, such as logo spacing. Keep the long guide, and open it only when a job needs it.

options.text: Upload the guide with no name or description, and let the model find the right pages by itself.
options.explanation: The model decides from the name and description whether to open a skill. With none, it has no reason to look inside.

questions.prompt: Which description makes the best door for the Tidewell kit?

options.text: Brand helper for all our design work, captions, and many other tasks that come up across clients and campaigns.
options.explanation: This is the kind of line OpenAI warns about. It does not say which brand or when to use it, like "Helps with legal work".
This is a file name, not a description. It says neither what the kit holds nor when to use it.

options.text: Holds the 40-page Tidewell guide: logo spacing, colour codes, photo rules, legal lines, voice, and page layouts.
options.explanation: It says what is inside but not when to use it. OpenAI's advice is to say both.

options.text: Tidewell kit: colours, logo rules, photo style, to use for every image, caption or banner made for Tidewell.
options.explanation: Right. It says what the kit holds and when to use it, which is the advice in OpenAI's Skills page.

questions.prompt: The card and the guide clash on stock photos. What is the best fix?

options.text: Add a line to the prompt: "If the card and the guide disagree, follow the guide." Both texts stay as they are.
options.explanation: The card stays wrong, and so does everyone who reads only the card. The clash is still there.

options.text: Ask the client which rule is true, write it once on the card, and change the guide so that both agree.
options.explanation: Right. This is our rule: one rule, one place. The model and the team then get the same answer.

options.text: Delete the stock-photo rule from both, so nothing can clash and the model uses its own judgment.
options.explanation: That removes a real brand rule. The client has a view on stock photos, and the kit should hold it.

options.text: Keep both. A model weighs the card against the guide and picks the more likely rule every time.
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs says it does this. Different requests can pick different rules, and the look drifts.
